claim_text: The dense basal planar defects are LPSO nanoplates: aggregates of four-layer Zn/Y-segregated fcc-type stacking faults, not conventional stacking faults

steps.observation: Bright-field TEM taken with g=0002 shows strong planar fault-like contrast lying on (0001), roughly ten plates per um
steps.image_note: the 'g 0002' arrow is drawn on the panel; the contrast is strong, whereas an R=1/3<10-10> fault would be extinct at g=0002

panels.caption_span: Bright-field TEM image showing the microstructure in the as-grown alloy was annealed at 520C for 5h followed by water quenching, and

steps.observation: HAADF-STEM: the plates appear as bright, heavy-atom-rich bands only a few atomic layers wide; the 1 nm inset resolves one such bright band
steps.image_note: at the 100 nm scale of the main panel individual atomic layers are not resolved; the inset shows a single bright band ~1-2 nm wide, consistent with but not proving four layers

panels.caption_span: Corresponding HAADF-STEM image. The inset shows a higher-magnification image. Zn/Y atoms are segregated along four atomic layers where an fcc-type stacking fault exists

closing_why: the claim names a fact no panel carries: Zn/Y as the segregating species; four-layer fcc-type fault stated in the caption
